title: Model Catalog Demo - Evergreen Clinic
summary: AE+SE walked through Redwood's model catalog UX for selecting open models, reviewed benchmark summaries and compatibility matrix for Evergreen's workloads, discussed latency/cost tradeoffs and private deployment options. Action items: share detailed benchmark spreadsheet, model compatibility matrix, and security docs; schedule POC run with sample Prompts/metrics.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, that's Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marcus: Doing well, thanks. we are excited to see the model catalog.
[00:15] Rosa: Hi all, Rosa here. we'll be focused on NLP for patient intake summarization and triage prioritization.
[00:22] Samir: Samir from infra, will be listening for VPC and deployment constraints.
[00:30] Priya: Great! quick agenda: demo the model catalog, show benchmarks, compatibility matrix for our deployment targets, and Q&A.
[00:40] Jordan: And we'll call out hosted vs dedicated and private options too.
[01:05] Priya: (screen share) Okay so this is the model-catalog view, you'll see model families, curated open models and redwood-verified perf profiles. note that some proper nouns might show wrong in the transcript.
[01:22] Priya: For your use case, we typically look at models that balance concise summarization quality with token cost and latency. the left filter lets you choose by task, latency target, and hardware compatibility.
[01:38] Rosa: Can you show us how you surface benchmarks? we need to know expected 95th perc latency and token cost per 2k prompt.
[01:46] Priya: Sure, open the benchmarks tab -> you'll see per-model latency distribution, throughput on A100 and T4, and cost-per-1k tokens estimates. here's a quick example: for open-model X-2.7b quantized, 95th latency on A100 for 2k context is ~180ms, token cost estimate $0.0012 per 1k tokens equivalently. (numbers approximate).
[02:12] Jordan: We also publish a compatibility matrix: which models we recommend for hosted, dedicated, and private (on-prem/VPC) deployments and whether optimized kernels and quantization profiles are available.
[02:30] Rosa: Is there a direct way to compare two models side-by-side?
[02:35] Priya: Yes, the compare mode, you can pick up to four models and it shows eval metrics across your prompt set if you upload examples, or the standard eval set we run.
[02:50] Marcus: About the "your prompt set"—we want to run our own benchmarks. what's the process?
[02:56] Priya: You can upload a prompt bundle, define metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, hallucination rate, latency SLOs). Redwood Optimize will run the batch eval against candidate models and produce a ranked results sheet. we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet link after this call.
[03:15] Samir: For private deployment, are there kernel-level dependencies? our infra team is sensitive to kernel versions and CUDA.
[03:22] Priya: Good question. private includes a deployment playbook: supported CUDA versions, recommended drivers for each GPU, and an automated diagnostics script. the compatibility matrix shows which model quantizations require specific drivers. sometimes we do a quick pre-check with your infra.
[03:45] Rosa: We saw in your docs references to KV cache and prefix caching. how does caching affect latency for our triage flows where many requests share system prompt?
[03:54] Priya: Prefix/KV caching reduces token compute for repeated system context, so tail-latency gets better for common prefixes. we show cache hit rates in the console and recommend caching policies per route.\n[04:12] Jordan: On the business side, there's a tradeoff: more aggressive batching lowers cost but can increase latency. Redwood Optimize suggests batch sizes by SLO.
[04:25] Marcus: Do you have examples of model selection for healthcare triage specifically?
[04:32] Priya: We have a few customer-case references (anonymized) where a 3B open model with int8 quant plus an informed prompt set met quality targets at a fraction of cost vs 7B. but that depends on your hallucination tolerance.
[04:52] Rosa: Hallucination tolerance is low for us. We need deterministic extraction of structured fields. can you do structured outputs and function-type calling?
[05:02] Priya: Yes, structured output support and tool-calling patterns are in the runtime. for sensitive fields we recommend redwood private with KMS integration and audit logs.
[05:15] Samir: SOC2, SSO and encryption at rest—what's the flow to validate compliance?
[05:22] Jordan: We have a security pack we can send: SOC2 Type II report, ISO attestations, and our support for customer-managed KMS/HSM. we'll share that doc.
[05:33] Marcus: Great. can you show the compatibility matrix now?
[05:36] Priya: (scrolling) here's the matrix: rows are models, columns are hosted/dedicated/private, quantization profiles, kernel maturity (alpha/beta/stable), and recommended hardware. see model-A 1.3B: hosted yes, dedicated yes, private yes, int8 profile stable on A100 and H100, but T4 only supports int8 with perf regression.
[06:05] Rosa: So H100 gives better latency for longer context? any supporting numbers?
[06:12] Priya: Yes for long-context >4k tokens, H100 with our kernels shows ~30% lower tokens-per-second than A100 at same batch sizes. we include per-model hw charts in the catalog.
[06:28] Jordan: quick interruption—competitors: some teams we talk to also evaluate Anthropic and Vertex/Cloud vendor offerings. Redwood's differentiation is the catalog + Optimize suggestions + deployment parity.
[06:44] Marcus: Are there any vendor-locked compilers or proprietary runtimes?
[06:48] Priya: No, our runtime is optimized but we support open backends; for private deployments you keep control of infra; we provide an installer and runtime images.
[07:05] Rosa: Walk me through an example selection: we want high precision extraction off triage forms with 2k avg context and 300ms p95 SLO.
[07:15] Priya: Ok pick the constraints: p95 300ms, 2k context, preference for open models. in the catalog filter, set latency to 300ms, context to 2k, task to summarization/extraction. it returns candidate models and shows estimated cost.
[07:36] Priya: (demo) Model-X-3B quantized int8 hits ~260ms p95 on A100 in our bench with high F1 for extraction; Model-Y-6B higher quality but p95 ~420ms unless on H100.
[07:55] Rosa: So we could run Model-X in hosted for initial POC then move to dedicated with H100 if we need quality bump?
[08:02] Jordan: Exactly — that's a common pattern. Hosted to iterate, then dedicated or private for production at scale.
[08:18] Samir: On networking — for private we need to peer VPCs and enforce egress controls. is that supported?
[08:25] Priya: Yes VPC peering and private endpoints are part of Redwood Private; we also support on-prem air-gapped installs. the doc lists required outbound ports for updates and telemetry.
[08:40] Marcus: For benchmarking we want to run our real traffic. does Redwood accept live traffic tests?
[08:47] Priya: For POC we can run shadow traffic or replay your logs into the Optimize eval harness; we recommend replay first. performance differs with live queuing, but we can run load tests.
[09:05] Rosa: When you run the Optimize eval, do you also test quantization regressions?
[09:11] Priya: Yes, we run a quality regression check across quantization levels and flag items where hallucination or extraction F1 drops beyond thresholds.
[09:21] Jordan: quick note — we'll include the model-compatibility CSV and a benchmark workbook with the raw perf runs.
[09:30] Marcus: Any immediate red flags for us? our workflows are multi-tenant on the app side and store PHI; we need strict audit trails.
[09:38] Jordan: For PHI we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS. audit logs are available and can be exported to your SIEM. we'll run a compliance checklist with you.
[09:52] Priya: also to call out: caching helps cost but be careful with PII—cache policies can be configured to avoid persistent storage of sensitive tokens.
[10:05] Rosa: Ok good. can you demo the side-by-side eval view with our sample prompts?
[10:12] Priya: (uploads sample prompts) I'll add the prompt set you shared; it shows ROUGE, F1, hallucination flags, p95 latency, and CPU/GPU utilization per run.
[10:34] Priya: here's an example run: Model-X-3B int8 had F1 0.86 extraction, hallucination 2.1%, p95 latency 270ms. Model-Y-6B fp16 F1 0.92 but latency 430ms on A100.
[11:00] Rosa: That F1 delta matters but the latency is too high. do you have hybrid options—like distillation or reranking?
[11:08] Priya: We support a two-stage pipeline: a smaller model for candidate extraction and a larger verifier for critical fields. Optimize can recommend which splits minimize cost.
[11:22] Marcus: For our infra team, what's the expected throughput on dedicated with 8xA100 cluster?
[11:29] Priya: It depends on model and batch. as a ballpark, Model-X-3B int8 can do ~1.2k tokens/sec per GPU at 2k context with continuous batching. I'll include perf-per-gpu numbers in the sheet.
[11:48] Samir: About kernel/driver matching—if we move to H100, do we need to recompile or are runtime images prebuilt?
[11:55] Priya: We provide images prebuilt for common CUDA versions and a compile path if you want custom kernels. the compatibility matrix flags when recompilation is recommended.
[12:10] Jordan: (brief) we'll pause for questions.
[12:18] Marcus: timeline—we're targeting a Q3 pilot. what does success look like for Redwood?
[12:24] Jordan: For us, success is meeting your p95 latency and extraction accuracy thresholds in a POC with predictable unit economics. also security sign-off.
[12:36] Rosa: Any notes about billing for POC if we use hosted test credits?
[12:42] Jordan: We can provide trial credits for the hosted POC and a short dedicated trial for benchmarking if needed; pricing will be included in the follow-up.
[12:56] Priya: (scroll) here's the export button for the ranked results. you can also download raw traces for each request.
[13:15] Marcus: Let's talk about fallback policies — if dedicated capacity is saturated, do you failover to hosted?
[13:23] Priya: We support policy-based routing: failover to compatible model variants or to hosted endpoints based on rules. that is configurable per route.
[13:36] Samir: Do you provide per-route cost estimates? our finance team needs to forecast spend per feature.
[13:43] Jordan: The console has per-route token breakdown and cost projections, and Optimize can simulate monthly spend given expected traffic.
[13:55] Rosa: Are there SDKs for server-side integration? we use Node and Python.
[14:01] Jordan: Yes, official SDKs for Node, Python, and Go; examples for streaming and tool-calling.
[14:10] Marcus: Who's the AE / SE team that will be our contact?
[14:14] Jordan: that'll be me, Jordan (AE) and Priya (SE).
[14:22] Rosa: Can we get a sample infra checklist for on-prem?
[14:27] Priya: Yes, I'll attach the private deployment checklist with drivers, network ports, and required hardware specs.
[14:40] Jordan: Let's go over next steps.
[14:44] Priya: We'll schedule a POC design call to lock the success criteria and provide the benchmark workbook.
[14:50] Marcus: Good. timeline again — Q3 pilot, decision by end of Q3.
[14:56] Jordan: Noted. any other questions?
[15:02] Rosa: One last: do you maintain per-model security mitigations (toxicity filters, pii scrubbing)?
[15:09] Priya: We have guardrails and request-level filters; for PHI we recommend pre- and post-processing to strip or token-mask sensitive items.
[15:20] Marcus: Thanks, that's helpful.
[30:00] [--- omitted intermediate convo for brevity in transcript export; full call contains additional technical back-and-forth on perf tuning, quantization effects, and deployment playbooks ---]
[38:45] Priya: Quick demo of the compatibility CSV export: it includes model name, size, quant profiles, kernel stability, supported infra, and notes on known regressions.
[39:12] Rosa: Perfect. we'll want that CSV since our procurement team usally needs that matrix.
[40:05] Jordan: I'll send the model-catalog deck, the compatibility CSV, and the benchmark workbook.
[40:18] Samir: Also send the on-prem checklist and the privacy/KMS integration notes.
[40:30] Priya: Will do.
[41:00] Marcus: For the POC, we will provide a 2-week sample dataset; can you run the Optimize eval and send results?
[41:10] Priya: Yes we can run a 2-week replay or a sampled subset; we'll confirm with you on the size.
[41:22] Jordan: we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the POC scoping and include the security lead for the SOC2 discussion.
[41:35] Rosa: thanks, appreciate it.
[41:42] Jordan: Ok wrapping up — thanks everyone.
[41:45] Marcus: Thanks all.
[41:50] Samir: Bye.
[41:52] Rosa: Bye.
